subtitle: Lesson 20 · Performance & Resource Estimation in Practice

steps.label: Running and interpreting a profiled VQE loop end to end
Projecting real-hardware shot and time budgets
Making a go/no-go call with calculated numbers
Reducing an infeasible plan to a feasible one

eyebrow: Step 1-2: profile small, project the real plan
code:
Toy: 2-qubit, p=2, 10 iterations
  classical 0.08s, sim 0.42s

Real target: p=4 (8 params),
150 iterations, 4096 shots/eval:
evals/gradient = 8*2 = 16
total_execs = 16*150 = 2,400
total_shots = 2,400*4,096
            = 9,830,400
caption: Close to 9.8 million shots is the real number a hardware-queue budget would need to absorb.

steps.label: Fewer iterations (150 -> 30)
steps.sub: Cuts shots 5x, but risks the optimizer not converging

steps.label: Fewer shots per eval (4096 -> 2048)
steps.sub: Halves shots, but doubles standard error on each gradient

steps.label: Train on simulator, validate on hardware
steps.sub: Usually the right answer — doesn't trade away either property

code:
Simulator: full 150-iter training,
  zero hardware-queue cost

Hardware: one final validation
  evaluation, 4096 shots

Real-hardware cost: 4,096 shots
  -- within the 2,000,000 budget
  by several orders of magnitude
caption: Doesn't trade away convergence quality or statistical precision to hit the budget.
